title: syn/yosys/run.sh never elaborates 6 of the 38 hdl/ modules, and re-parses all.v 32 times to do it
body:
`syn/yosys/run.sh` exists to enforce `hdl/README` rule 2 — *sv2v + yosys must
elaborate every top* — and its own header says the `tops` array is the
authoritative list. Six of the 38 modules in `hdl/` are not in it, and are
never elaborated by any run. Separately, the script re-parses the whole design
once per top, which is where its 40 seconds go.

The two are the same mechanism, which is why they belong in one issue: the
redundant re-parse is currently the only thing giving those six modules any
front-end coverage at all. Fix the speed first and you delete the coverage
silently.

Found while profiling Yosys for kebag-logic/milan-fpga#286.

## 1. Six modules are never elaborated

`hdl/` declares 38 modules across 42 `.sv` files. The `tops` array names 32.
Running `hierarchy -top <T>` for each of those 32 and taking the union of the
modules that survive gives exactly those same 32. The six below are not
reached transitively as a submodule of any top either.

Never elaborated by any top:

- `KL_acmp_nvm_shadow`
- `KL_mrp_strip`
- `KL_pp_dispatch_fifo`
- `KL_srp_admission`
- `KL_srp_top`
- `protocol_processor_top`

This is a gap, not a latent defect: all six elaborate cleanly today. Running
the gate's own program on each —
`read_verilog all.v; hierarchy -check -top <T>; proc; opt_clean` — gives
`ELABORATES OK` for all six.

It is worth noting which module is on that list. `protocol_processor_top` is
the subject of #22, whose 44 use-before-declaration identifiers were found by
the *integrator's* Vivado front end, not by this gate — because this gate has
never made it a top.

Why nothing has failed yet: `read_verilog all.v` parses and AST-elaborates
**every** module in the file, whether or not the selected top uses it. So a
syntax error in `KL_srp_top` does currently fail all 32 runs. What is missing
is `hierarchy -check`, `proc` and `opt_clean` on those six — the part that
catches an unresolved instance, a missing parameter, or a surviving vendor
primitive.

## 2. The design is parsed 32 times

`sv2v` lowers all of `hdl/` into one 21,912-line `all.v` (652 KB), and the
script then starts 32 separate `yosys` processes, each of which begins with
`read_verilog all.v`. Measured on one box (`yosys 0.66`, `sv2v 0.0.13`);
`sv2v` is 5.1 s on top of every variant and is unchanged by all of them:

| variant | wall | peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A — as shipped: 32 processes, each `read_verilog all.v` | 39.65 s | 200 MiB |
| B — one process, parse once, `design -save` / `design -load` per top | 9.34 s | 232 MiB |
| C — 32 processes, `read_verilog -defer` | 10.31 s | 128 MiB |
| D — 16-way process pool, `read_verilog -defer` | **1.25 s** | 129 MiB |

Same 32 tops, same checks, same result in every variant.

## 3. The trap: C and D would delete the coverage described in section 1

`read_verilog -defer` postpones elaboration of modules the selected top does
not instantiate. That is exactly why it is fast, and exactly why it must not
be applied first: the six modules in section 1 would stop being parsed at all,
and the gap would go from "not fully checked" to "not checked".

So the order is fixed:

1. add the six modules to the `tops` array;
2. then make it fast.

Done in that order, both numbers improve. Measured with all 38 modules as
tops:

| variant | tops | wall | peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| as shipped today | 32 | 39.65 s | 200 MiB |
| A — same structure, 38 tops | 38 | 52.60 s | 286 MiB |
| D — 16-way pool + `-defer`, 38 tops | **38** | **5.68 s** | 281 MiB |

Six more modules covered, and **−86%** wall time against what the gate costs
today.

## Proposed change

- Extend `tops` with `KL_acmp_nvm_shadow`, `KL_mrp_strip`,
  `KL_pp_dispatch_fifo`, `KL_srp_admission`, `KL_srp_top` and
  `protocol_processor_top`, so the array means what its header says.
- Add a check that fails the gate when a module is declared in `hdl/` and is
  not in `tops` — otherwise the same six reappear one commit at a time. The
  array is only authoritative if something enforces it.
- Then convert the loop to a bounded process pool with `read_verilog -defer`,
  with one result line per top so a failure still names the module. `set -eu`
  plus `exit 1` on the first failure does not survive a pool unchanged.
- Keep the `synth_xilinx` / `select -assert-count 6 t:RAMB36E1` regression
  gate exactly as it is; it is a second, separate invocation and none of this
  touches it.

If a pool is judged too much change for this script, variant B (one process,
`design -save` / `design -load`) gets 39.65 s to 9.34 s with no concurrency
and no `-defer`, so it keeps full parse coverage even for modules that are not
tops. That is the conservative option and it is still a 4x improvement.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every module declared under `hdl/` is a top in `tops`, and a check
      fails the gate if that ever stops being true.
- [ ] The gate still fails on a deliberately broken module — prove it by
      breaking one of the six newly added tops and watching the gate go red,
      not by observing that it is green.
- [ ] A failure names the module it failed on, under whatever concurrency is
      adopted.
- [ ] The `RAMB36E1` count assertion is unchanged and still passes.
- [ ] The PR reports before/after wall time and the top count, both measured
      on the same machine.

## Notes on reproducing

```sh
# module census vs the tops array
grep -rhoE '^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*' hdl --include='*.sv' \
  | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u

# reachability: union of what survives hierarchy -top over the current tops
yosys -q -p "read_verilog all.v; hierarchy -top <T>; tee -q -o ls.<T> ls"

# the four variants, against one sv2v output staged as the script stages it
yosys -q -p "read_verilog all.v; hierarchy -check -top <T>; proc; opt_clean"
yosys -q -p "read_verilog -defer all.v; hierarchy -check -top <T>; proc; opt_clean"
yosys -q -p "read_verilog all.v; design -save RD; design -load RD; hierarchy -check -top <T>; proc; opt_clean; ..."
```

Timings above are from one box and are not a pass criterion; the coverage gap
is. Reproduce with the tool versions stated (`yosys 0.66`, `sv2v 0.0.13`),
because this repository's own `portability` job pins neither:

```yaml
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y yosys
curl -sL https://github.com/zachjs/sv2v/releases/latest/download/sv2v-Linux.zip
```

`apt-get install yosys` on `ubuntu-latest` currently resolves to 0.33, and
`releases/latest` is whatever `sv2v` shipped most recently. Both ends of the
front end float. The integrator has the same Yosys problem and is tracking it
in kebag-logic/milan-fpga#287; the `sv2v` half is specific to this workflow
and would be worth pinning in the same change.
